# Changelog

## November 13, 2026

1. 23:00 UTC

### autor api -d - reads the request body from stdin

```
echo '{"title": "Copy started", "kind": "note"}' |
  autor api post /missions/exp003/updates -d -
```

The CLI reference says that `-d -` reads the JSON body from stdin. Before this change, `autor` read the `-` as the body and stopped with `--data is not valid JSON`. Now it reads stdin. If stdin is empty, `autor` stops and tells you.

The fix arrives with `autor` 0.29.1, so run `autor upgrade` first.

## October 30, 2026

1. 23:30 UTC

### An ended cluster frees its private network at once

You say to your agent

> “Delete cluster exp003, then make a new two-node InfiniBand cluster named exp004.”

Each InfiniBand cluster makes a private network for itself. Before this change, that network stayed for seven days after the cluster ended, because the addresses of its detached nodes were in quarantine, and it counted against the workspace limit of eight networks the whole time. Short runs filled the limit in days.

Now we delete an ended cluster's network as soon as no node is attached to it, usually within a minute of the delete. A node of your own that you attached to that network keeps it until you detach the node.

The same rule applies to every private network: a network with no attached node deletes at once, quarantine or not. The seven-day quarantine still keeps a detached address from going to another node in the same network. See Private networks and Clusters.

## October 20, 2026

1. 19:10 UTC

### A node restores from a snapshot faster

You say to your agent

> “Make a new H100 node from my latest snapshot and start the training run.”

A node that restores from a snapshot now downloads it through more parallel connections. The host uses one connection for each of its CPU cores, from 8 to 64 connections. Before this change, every host used 8 connections. A snapshot of less than 128 MiB still downloads through one connection.

In most restores, the download now also writes the disk directly. Before this change, the node unpacked the snapshot onto its disk after the download ended. In the two weeks before this change, that step took 85 seconds on average, and the download took 69 seconds. The platform still checks the snapshot's sha256 checksum, and the node gets its disk only after the check passes.

`restore_progress` on `get_node` shows the connections in use in `lanes`. See Snapshots.

## October 19, 2026

1. 18:30 UTC

### Queued cpu-8 work gets another machine

You say to your agent

> “Run these 12 preprocessing jobs on cpu-8 and tell me when they finish.”

When cpu-8 work waits for room, we now start another machine for it. A cpu-8 job counts after it waits 10 minutes for a slot. A new cpu-8 node counts after it waits 3 minutes in the queue. The machine takes a few minutes to start, and then the work that waits starts on it. The number of extra machines has a limit, so a very large queue can still wait.

Jobs got this change on October 16, and nodes got it on October 19. Before October 16, cpu-8 jobs could wait in the queue for more than an hour when nodes used every cpu-8 slot.

We stop the extra machine after nothing runs on it for 30 minutes. We never stop your node to do this. Before we stop the machine, we save the disk of each stopped node on it to storage. The next wake of such a node restores the disk on a different machine, so it takes longer than a usual wake. See Queue.

## October 17, 2026

1. 07:15 UTC

### A restore continues after you stop the node

You say to your agent

> “Wake my 80 GB node. If it is not ready in 15 minutes, stop it and try again later.”

If you stop a node while it restores from a snapshot, the next wake of the node now goes back to the same host if that host has room. The host keeps the downloaded parts that passed the checksum check for 6 hours, and the restore continues from those parts. On a different host, the download starts again from the beginning.

Before this change, a wake after such a stop could go to a different host or lose the kept parts. Then the download started from zero. A node with a large snapshot that was stopped before each restore ended could never finish its restore.

Do not stop a node to retry a restore that still runs. Read `restore_progress.hint` on `get_node`. The hint tells you when to wait and when the restore no longer runs. See Snapshots.

## October 15, 2026

1. 21:45 UTC

### The metadata service answers as soon as a node starts

You say to your agent

> “Start a cpu-2 node, run my script, and stop the node from inside when the script ends.”

Code on a node can now call the metadata service as soon as the node starts. The node's metadata now arrives about one second after the start, and a call in that time waits for it, up to 5 seconds. Before this change, `GET /v1/node` and `POST /v1/stop` could return HTTP 503 for up to 10 seconds after the node started. An on-wake command often runs in that time.

If the metadata does not arrive in 5 seconds, the call returns HTTP 503 with `metadata temporarily unavailable; retry`. Retry that response with a bounded wait. Give `POST /v1/stop` a timeout of more than 10 seconds.

HTTP 403 has two causes. The request does not have the header `Metadata-Flavor: givemeanode`, or the request does not come from the container itself. If your code uses an HTTP proxy, set `NO_PROXY=169.254.42.1,metadata.givemeanode.internal`. See Metadata.
2. 01:00 UTC

### We tell you when we cancel a price increase

You say to your agent

> “Is the H100 price increase that you announced still on?”

If we cancel a price increase that we announced, the dashboard shows a notice that says so. Each organization that got the email about the increase gets a second email that cancels it. The email includes the text of the first one. See Rates.

1. 23:00 UTC
